industry.why: Neutral at industry level, carried, with the sector rows carrying a view that moved inside the industry this week: Software B2B Enterprise goes to Neutral on the rotation into software, Semiconductors stays Underweight on the AI capital spending re-pricing, Hardware stays Neutral with the evidence moved against it at the margin. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): the market has stopped paying for AI capital spending (hyperscaler prints gave no lift, ABB sold on data-centre orders) while demand is intact and sub-sector upgrades continue (memory, equipment, power electronics), and the software-against-semiconductors factor pair is reversing (Goldman Sachs' desk, 26 October). Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: B now, B prior. The industry row stays C because the industry is split by the rotation itself. Counter-case for D: the Nasdaq down 6% in two weeks with momentum down 15% is a regime statement about this industry; for B: the only industry with upgrades inside the sell-off.

sector.why: Underweight, carried, with the tape now agreeing: Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-11-06 against 2026-09-04, not week on week: D now, A prior, the sharpest fall in technology, where last week's reading still ranked the sector B. The two conditions for Neutral (the AI credit channel stabilising; a second house joining Jefferies' European call) could not be tested because no strategist reached the pack; the only artificial-intelligence item is an undated headline that low AI exposure is Europe's edge. Component 1 regime, 6-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its high, now present in Europe's own prices: the STOXX Europe 600 0.9% from its 52-week high with the share of stocks above the 100, 150 and 200-day averages at or below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows, breadth recovering for a second week; the causes, inflation, rates, yields, credit and the consumer, unread this week because the strategist and newsletter files did not reach the pack, so the credit-and-cost-of-debt read of 30-Oct-26 with the US ten-year above 5% is held one week stale; sources present 2026-W45, headline-only). Of the Pool's semiconductor names, Technoprobe, AT&S, INFICON, Sensirion, STMicroelectronics, Soitec, AIXTRON and AMS Osram are marked leaving the Pool or meet a Sell Criterion, so the row's cost to the Lists is falling of its own accord. Counter-case: demand was never the problem and European exposure is equipment, power and optics. To C when the AI credit channel is read stable or a second house joins the European call, with relative strength holding C or better.

geography.why: Underweight, carried unchanged with the reason strengthened. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): the spillover from France to Italy is the new fact this week (Goldman, 16 Oct, 'tentative spillover to Italy'), and the Italian listings in the Pool are bank-heavy (Monte dei Paschi, Credito Emiliano, Mediobanca) beside global businesses (Eni, Saipem, Tenaris, STMicroelectronics, Technoprobe, Reply). Not Double Underweight because Goldman also says contagion risk is lower than in 2011-15, its fragmentation index shows risk 'remains limited', and Southern European banks are healthier; relative strength is not graded by country. Moves to F if the fragmentation index rises or the Italian premium is read above 150 basis points; back to C under 100.

memo.verdict: Park. Neutral on the shares at EUR 33.08 (2026-10-01): bullish on the business, bearish on the price. Technoprobe is a 'Demand Inflection' that has already happened and has already been paid for; the modal total shareholder return from EUR 33.08 is about -10.9 percent a year over eighteen months (to 2028-04-02, value including cash returns 27.81 EUR) and about -5.1 percent a year over three years (to 2029-10-02, value 28.25 EUR), an F on the framework's anchors. The case is parked on return, not on the gate line: management B, business quality A, predictability (Transmission) A and trackability (Leading indicators) B do not trigger the park rule. Re-open levels: about EUR 23 (a C return on our path) and about EUR 21 (the 20 percent a year bar); about EUR 16 clears the bar over three years. Triggers to re-open: the Q3 2026 results on 2026-11-11, a further capacity announcement, FormFactor's qualification at Nvidia, TSMC advanced-node utilisation, the dollar. Conviction medium on the earnings path (a working hypothesis built from guidance and consensus, not a Viewforth model), high on the valuation arithmetic. At EUR 33.08 we would be betting that AI test intensity, Nvidia's sole-sourcing and a top-quartile multiple all hold for eighteen months, which we rate unlikely; below about EUR 21 to 23 we would be betting only that the structural half of the test-intensity story is real.
case: A sector-level change in the physics of chip testing (power, pad pitch, chiplets) has made test content per AI accelerator rise faster than accelerator units, so probe card consumption grows at a multiple of chip units; Deutsche Bank models Technoprobe's AI GPU probe card sales compounding at 130 percent over 2023 to 2026E against GPU units of about 50 percent. The force is sector-level and externally confirmed (Advantest's 19 percent market raise with 18 months' visibility; Teradyne's raised outlook; TSMC's advanced nodes near 100 percent utilisation through 2027; hyperscaler capital spending toward USD 1 trillion by 2028) and the company recorded an order backlog for the first time in its history, with commitments into 2027, so the 'Demand Inflection' test (sector-level; structural or cyclical with two-plus years' visibility; evidenced by industry data and customer capital spending) is met. It is a tailwind on five of seven external forces and a headwind on two: competition from 2027 (FormFactor's Texas plant ramping H1 2027 with Nvidia and TSMC enforcing multi-vendor qualification) and currency (EUR 30m off H1 2026 revenue, EUR 23m off EBITDA). Change Forces A.

Technoprobe, sole supplier of vertical MEMS probe cards to Nvidia and holder of over 60 percent of non-memory vertical MEMS, captured the change almost entirely. The internal change is real but follows the demand: capital expenditure raised to EUR 350m through Q1 2027 for a 140 percent capacity increase and a EUR 1.6bn run-rate, guidance raised twice in three months (mid-teens growth to EUR 1,050m to 1,100m, EBITDA margin to 46 to 48 percent), four product lines resourced and dated, no red flag present (no caretaker chief executive, no 'PowerPoint transformation', no crown jewel sold, no debt, no debt-funded buyback). Internal forces B, because management's contribution is to have built the capacity to meet an external force, which is necessary but not itself a change.

The change has travelled every layer of the 'Six Layer Inputs-outputs' chain: resources (the capacity build), choices (targets pulled forward twice), actions (35 percent capacity added in one quarter by internal tooling), key operating metrics (utilisation over 90 percent, the backlog), financial statements (H1 2026 revenue +42.4 percent, EBITDA margin 44.4 percent from 32.6 percent, net profit +315 percent) and the sell-side's estimates (FY2026 consensus EPS +140.5 percent over twelve months; seven of seven Buy). Financial Outputs A. Key metrics A under the framework's conditional rule: the near-term metrics are 'very positive', so only plausible logic for continuation is needed, which exists in the backlog, the EUR 1.6bn run-rate from Q1 2027 and the new lines dated for 2027 and 2028; cash conversion C is a one-off capacity build carried by net cash. Sell-side upgrades B: further upgrades over six to twelve months are probable on the record (four beats, two raises, implied Q4 guidance judged conservative) and the skew (no cuts, FY2026 and FY2027 EPS up 19 to 20 percent in three months), but consensus FY2026 revenue (EUR 1,097m) sits at the top of guidance, consensus FY2027 already assumes the expanded capacity full, and our own path is at the consensus mean for FY2027 and in the bottom quarter of the range for FY2028, so the upgrades are modest and the attribute cannot be A where the house view is not above the street. Goldilocks growth C: modal EPS growth is far above the 12 to 20 percent band (over 200 percent over six months, about 47 percent over eighteen months, 23.6 percent a year over three years), which the framework marks down hard above 40 percent; the inflection is the point of the pattern, which is why C and not D. Staircase B: dated steps (Q3 results 2026-11-11; a capacity step toward EUR 2.1bn to 2.4bn expected in H2 2026; HBM qualification at two more vendors by end-2026; the plant complete and EUR 1.6bn run-rate by Q1 2027; HBM4E in 2027; first Eclipse orders 2027), with a negative step of equal weight in the same window (FormFactor Texas, H1 2027).
counter_case: At its strongest, the counter-case is the sell-side's: consensus is still structurally too low, as it has been for eighteen months, and the record proves it. FY2026 revenue expectations went from about EUR 720m in March 2026 to EUR 1,097m in October; the company has beaten its guidance midpoint every quarter for five quarters, raised its full year twice in three months, and surpassed its FY2028 Capital Markets Day targets in FY2026; it lost no share at the key account through H1 2026 despite FormFactor's qualification attempts; it holds a backlog it has never had before. Deutsche Bank's FY2028 EBIT sits 40 percent above the street, on EUR 2.2bn of revenue at a 55 percent EBITDA margin; a capacity tripling to a EUR 2.1bn to 2.4bn annual run-rate is expected to be announced in H2 2026; HBM at EUR 250m by 2028 and silicon photonics at over EUR 300m by 2030 are not yet in most models. On that path the 24-month-forward earnings are nearer EUR 1.5 than EUR 1.0, the stock is on about 22x, not 37x, and the return is an A even at the stock's own median multiple: the consensus path to FY2029 EPS of EUR 1.48 at 27x gives EUR 39.96 and about 13.4 percent a year, and at 32.3x EUR 47.80 and about 27.8 percent a year. The record's own FY2027 estimate sits at the consensus mean, not below it; the sell-side's EV/EBIT cross-check puts the stock in line with FormFactor and BE Semiconductor on CY2028; and if the capacity step is announced and filled, the record's FY2028 is too low by 10 percent or more. The record concedes all of this, and that the direction of error has been one way for eighteen months.

On the Foundations, the counter is the leadership research's: a family-controlled, narrowly-led, insider-promoted company with a documented history of process gaps in its own fab and a 2023 record of failing to supply an upturn, attempting a 140 percent capacity expansion in fifteen months under customers who want a second source, is a C, not a B. The record concedes eight of ten directors from the family list, the family's sale after the upgrade, the untested chief executive, the founders' sons exempt from variable pay, and the expert evidence; it holds B on the delivery since April 2024 and carries the execution risk at Riskiness.
triggers: - Re-open levels: about EUR 23 (eighteen-month return a C on our path) and about EUR 21 (the 20 percent a year bar); about EUR 16 clears the bar over three years. A disappointment that resets the multiple is the other way in.

- Invalidate levels (the earnings review's exit signals, adopted): TSMC advanced-node utilisation below 85 to 90 percent for three months; a quarterly revenue decline of more than 20 percent; gross margin below 50 percent for two quarters; lead times beyond 14 weeks; FormFactor's qualification announced at Nvidia with volume.

- The Q3 2026 results on 2026-11-11 against guidance of EUR 314m revenue, 52.0 percent EBITDA margin and 61.5 percent gross margin (tolerances plus or minus 3 percent and 200 basis points); whether the Q4 2026 GPU production pause (implied Q4 EBITDA margin about 49 percent) is confirmed as one quarter; backlog commentary and any sign of double-ordering.

- Whether a further capacity step beyond the EUR 1.6bn run-rate (Deutsche Bank expects EUR 2.1bn to 2.4bn by FY2028) is announced in H2 2026; consensus FY2028 revenue of EUR 1,953m needs it, our EUR 1,800m does not. If announced and filled, our FY2028 is too low by 10 percent or more.

- Nvidia share: FormFactor's Apollo qualification and Texas ramp statements (H1 2027); Technoprobe gross margin and lead times as the read-through; a loss of 10 to 20 percent by 2028 is our modal case, material loss before H1 2027 unlikely.

- The margin: FY2027 about 50 percent plausible (consensus 51.0), FY2028 slipping toward 48 percent probable (consensus 51.6); a Q3 print at or above 52 percent with the Q4 step-down explained away would move us.
